title: Patch: the pack-opening scene takes and returns focus and closes on Escape like the game's other dialogs

**Issue #1757 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1757: Patch: the pack-opening scene takes and returns focus and closes on Escape like the game's other dialogs
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The pack-opening scene is a full-screen modal, but it ignores the keyboard: Escape does nothing, focus is never moved into it, Tab walks the inert page behind it, and its only exit — the Close button — is disabled while a pack is still opening, so a keyboard player whose open request stalls has no way out at all. After the change it behaves like every other overlay in the game: focus moves in, stays in, comes back out, and Escape closes it when closing is allowed.

## Why

`PackScene` is portalled to `document.body` with `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` (`apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx:212-219`) but installs no keyboard or focus handling — no initial focus, no trap, no restore, no Escape — while every other overlay uses `useModalOverlay` (`apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts:150-207`) or hand-rolls the same (`settings/SettingsPanel.tsx:166-228`, `tutorial/TutorialResult.tsx:127-136`). Its Close button is disabled while `busy` (`PackOpening.tsx:316`), which a hung `openPack` request makes a real trap.

## Proposal

Wrap the scene in the shared overlay behaviour — focus on open, a Tab trap, focus restoration on close, and Escape honouring `busy` exactly as Close does.

## Where it lands

`apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx`; the shared `useModalOverlay` behaviour in `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts` or its owning module; vitest beside the pack tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Focus enters the scene on open and returns to the opener on close
- [ ] Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog
- [ ] Escape closes it unless `busy` — matching the Close button's disabled state
- [ ] Mouse and reduced-motion behaviour are unchanged

## Size and risks

Small–medium — one component adopting an existing pattern; the only judgment is whether a hung open should offer a cancel, which the `busy` rule already answers.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40056879121)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`PackScene` (`apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx`) behaves like the game's other modal overlays by adopting the shared `useModalOverlay` hook (`apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts`). When the scene opens, focus moves onto it. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it and pull back focus that has escaped. Escape closes it unless `busy`, exactly when Close is disabled. On close, focus returns to the Open / Open all button that opened it. Mouse, touch, swipe, hold and reduced-motion behaviour stay as they are, and the existing tests stay green unedited.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts` | change | `trapTab`: focus on the dialog element itself counts as outside. `useModalOverlay`: new optional third parameter `closable = true`; while it is false, Escape and `close` do nothing. Doc comments. |
| `apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx` | change | Header comment, an import of `useModalOverlay`, a `sceneRef`, the hook call in `PackScene`, and `ref`/`tabIndex={-1}` on the scene's root `div`. |
| `apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.test.tsx` | change | A new `describe("#1757 …")` block with six tests. |

Do not touch: anything outside `apps/web/src/`; the hook's other users (`CardDetail.tsx`, `InspectSheet.tsx`, `CardList.tsx`, `FaceDown.tsx`, `StackSheet.tsx`, `emotes/HeroInspect.tsx`); `SettingsPanel.tsx`; `TutorialResult.tsx`; `packs.css`; `apps/web/src/i18n/` (no new strings); `spec/`; `crates/`; `e2e/`. No spec section governs this. It is client presentation (SPEC §14.3/§14.4 only say what the scene shows) and CLAUDE.md rule 7 is untouched. The hook's existing R279 tooltip check stays as it is. No new ruling, no patch fragment.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts`, `trapTab`** (lines 121–142). Replace
   `const outside = active === null || !dialog.contains(active);`
   with
   `const outside = active === null || active === dialog || !dialog.contains(active);`
   Append to the doc comment above `trapTab`: `Focus on the dialog itself (the pack scene's root holds it from the open, #1757) counts as outside, so the next Tab goes to the first control and Shift+Tab to the last.` (No current user's dialog root can take focus: none of them has a `tabIndex`, so their behaviour is unchanged.)

2. **Same file, `useModalOverlay`** (lines 144–207).
   - Change the signature to:
     ```ts
     export function useModalOverlay(
       onClose: () => void,
       focusRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>,
       closable = true,
     ): ModalOverlay {
     ```
   - Below `const onCloseRef = useRef(onClose);`, add `const closableRef = useRef(closable);`.
   - In the dependency-less `useLayoutEffect` that sets `onCloseRef.current = onClose;`, add `closableRef.current = closable;` on the next line.
   - In `onKeyDown`, directly after `if (event.key !== "Escape") return;`, add:
     ```ts
     // A dialog that cannot close now (the pack scene while its open is out, #1757) ignores Escape.
     if (!closableRef.current) return;
     ```
     The guard comes before `restoreFocus`, so focus is not pulled out of a dialog that stays open.
   - Make the first line of `close` `if (!closableRef.current) return;`.
   - Append to the hook's doc comment: `While \`closable\` is false (the pack scene while its open request is out, #1757), Escape and \`close\` do nothing, as that dialog's disabled Close does.`

3. **`apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.tsx`, header comment.** After the `REDUCED MOTION …` paragraph (line 15), add a blank `//` line and then:
   ```
   // THE KEYBOARD (#1757): the scene is a modal overlay as the inspect views are (`useModalOverlay`): its
   // root takes the focus when it opens and gives it back to the opener when it closes, Tab and Shift+Tab
   // stay inside it, and Escape closes it unless an open request is out, when Close is disabled too.
   ```

4. **Same file, imports.** After `import { CardBack, CardFace, faceModel } from "../cards/index.ts";`, add `import { useModalOverlay } from "../cards/inspect/store.ts";`.

5. **Same file, `PackScene` body.** Directly after `const domRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);` (line 97), add:
   ```ts
   const sceneRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);

   // Focus moves in on open and back out on close, Tab stays inside, and Escape closes as Close does: not while busy.
   useModalOverlay(onClose, sceneRef, !busy);
   ```
   Ignore the return value. The Close button keeps `onClick={onClose}`. When the panel unmounts the scene, the hook's cleanup gives focus back.

6. **Same file, the root `div` in `createPortal`** (lines 213–221). After `aria-label={title}`, add `ref={sceneRef}` and `tabIndex={-1}`. Change nothing else in the JSX.

7. Write the tests below, then run the commands in **Tests**.

## Tests

File: `apps/web/src/packs/PackOpening.test.tsx`. Append one new top-level block at the end of the file, `describe("#1757 the pack-opening scene's focus and keys", () => { … })`. It uses real timers: no `vi.useFakeTimers()`, because the panel tests `await`. Inside it, add this helper (copied from `cards/inspect/inspect.test.tsx:1073`):

```ts
/** fireEvent returns false when a handler called preventDefault. */
function tabFrom(element: Element, shift = false): boolean {
  return fireEvent.keyDown(element, { key: "Tab", shiftKey: shift });
}
```

Use the file's existing `props()`, `panel()`, `packsServer()`, `T`, `openedPack`, `writeSettings` and `Reply`. Keep every R-id out of test titles and comments; `#1757` is fine.

1. `it("#1757 the scene takes the focus when it opens, and Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it", …)`
   - Render a fragment: `<button type="button" data-testid="behind">behind</button>` followed by `<PackScene {...props()} />`.
   - Let `scene = getByTestId(T.scene)`, `pack = getByTestId(T.pack)`, `close = getByTestId(T.close)`.
   - Expect `scene` toHaveFocus.
   - `tabFrom(scene)` is `false` and `pack` has focus.
   - `tabFrom(pack, true)` is `false` and `close` has focus.
   - `tabFrom(close)` is `false` and `pack` has focus.
   - `scene.focus()`, then `tabFrom(scene, true)` is `false` and `close` has focus.
   - `pack.focus()`, then `tabFrom(pack)` is `true` (a Tab between two controls inside is left to the browser).
   - `behind.focus()`, then `tabFrom(behind)` is `false` and `pack` has focus.
2. `it("#1757 while an open is out nothing in it can take the focus, so Tab and Shift+Tab keep it on the scene", …)`
   - Render `<PackScene {...props({ busy: true })} />`.
   - Expect the scene to have focus.
   - `tabFrom(scene)` is `false` and the scene still has focus.
   - `tabFrom(scene, true)` is `false` and the scene still has focus.
3. `it("#1757 Escape closes the scene, but not while an open is out, when Close is disabled too", …)`
   - `const given = props({ busy: true })`, then `const { rerender } = render(<PackScene {...given} />)`.
   - `fireEvent.keyDown(scene, { key: "Escape" })`. Expect `given.onClose` not to have been called, `T.close` to be disabled and the scene to have focus.
   - `rerender(<PackScene {...given} busy={false} />)`. Expect `T.close` to be enabled.
   - Escape again. Expect `given.onClose` to have been called once.
4. `it("#1757 under reduced motion the scene takes the focus and Escape closes it the same", …)`
   - `writeSettings({ reduceMotion: true })`, then `const given = props({ opened: openedPack() })` and render it.
   - Expect `T.scene` to have `data-motion="reduce"` and to have focus.
   - Escape. Expect `given.onClose` to have been called once.
5. `it("#1757 focus goes back to the Open button that opened the scene, on Escape and on Done", async …)`
   - `packsServer()`, then `await panel()`.
   - `const opener = getByTestId(T.open("Core"))`, then `opener.focus()` and `fireEvent.click(opener)`. Expect the scene to have focus.
   - Escape on the scene. Expect `queryByTestId(T.scene)` to be null and `opener` to have focus.
   - `fireEvent.click(opener)`, `fireEvent.click(getByTestId(T.skipAll))`, then `await screen.findByTestId(T.outcome(0))`. Expect `T.close` to have the text "Done", then click it.
   - Expect the scene to be gone and `getByTestId(T.open("Core"))` to have focus. Core still has one pack, so its row stays.
6. `it("#1757 the next pack of a batch takes the focus again", async …)`
   - Set up the server as the existing batch test does: `packsServer({ open: (call): Reply => ({ status: 200, body: { ...openedPack(), unopened: call === 1 ? 1 : 0 } satisfies OpenedPackResponse }) })`, then `await panel()`.
   - Click `T.openAll("Core")`, click `T.skipAll`, then `await screen.findByTestId(T.outcome(0))`. Click `T.next`.
   - Expect `T.pack` to have `data-state="sealed"` and `T.scene` to have focus.

Commands (from the repository root):

```
sh scripts/build-wasm.sh                                             # once: the web tests import src/wasm/pkg
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/packs/PackOpening.test.tsx
pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/cards/inspect src/cards/wheel src/emotes src/packs src/game/ConfirmConcede.test.tsx
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/packs apps/web/src/cards/inspect/store.ts
```

The second vitest line runs every other user of the hook: they must pass unchanged. On the unchanged base, that line passes all 271 tests.

## Done when

- [ ] Focus enters the scene on open and returns to the opener on close (tests 1, 5, 6)
- [ ] Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the dialog, busy included (tests 1, 2)
- [ ] Escape closes the scene unless `busy`, matching Close's disabled state (test 3)
- [ ] Mouse and reduced-motion behaviour are unchanged: every existing test in `PackOpening.test.tsx` and `PackObject.test.tsx` passes unedited, and test 4 passes
- [ ] The hook's other users' tests pass unchanged (the second vitest line)
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint on the touched paths are clean
- [ ] The harness's checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy and cargo tests are untouched by this change but must stay green, and the web tests with `--changed origin/main`

## Risks

- **The other overlays.** `useModalOverlay` is shared by six other components. `closable` defaults to `true`. The `trapTab` change only matters when the dialog element itself holds focus, and no existing dialog root is focusable. The second vitest line proves both.
- **Hidden information and rule 7.** Nothing changes. The scene still renders only the server's answer, and Escape goes through the panel's `close`, which already refuses while `busy`.
- **Batch remount.** `PackScene` is keyed by `round`, so Next pack unmounts the old scene and mounts a new one. The old scene's cleanup restores focus to the opener if it is still on the page. The new scene focuses its own root either way (test 6).
- **An opener that is gone.** Opening the last pack of a kind removes its row, and a count dropping to 1 removes Open all. Focus then has nowhere to return, and `restoreFocus` leaves it on `<body>`, as every overlay does. Do not add a fallback target. It is out of scope.
- **The focus ring.** Do not add CSS. The root is focused programmatically after a mouse click on Open, so it does not match `:focus-visible`, and mouse users see no ring. SettingsPanel and ConfirmConcede focus a `tabIndex={-1}` root the same way, with no outline rule.
- **`spec check`.** An R-id in a new test title or comment would make that test claim to prove a ruling. Use `#1757` only.

## Open questions

None block the build. These decisions were settled here, and a person may overrule them:

- **The scene's root takes focus on open**, not the pack button or Close. The pack button unmounts once the cards show, and the hook finds the dialog through this ref on every Tab and Escape. Focusing Close would let Enter close the scene at once.
- **The `busy` rule lives in the shared hook** as the optional `closable` parameter. The rejected alternative was a second window listener in `PackScene` that stops the hook's: it depends on registration order and hides the rule from the hook.
- **No cancel for a hung open.** The issue says the `busy` rule answers this: Escape stays off while Close is disabled.
- **No `.pack-scene:focus` outline rule.** That is visual tuning the task does not ask for.
- **No ruling.** Overlay focus is presentation, not a game rule (ConfirmConcede and B25 had none). No card plays differently, so there is no patch fragment.
````
